nodes.summary: For $b > 0$ and every $m$, $\int_{\mathbb{R}} \exp(-|z - m| / b) / (2b) \, dz = 1$: translate to $m = 0$, use the symmetry $z \mapsto |z|$ to reduce to $2 \int_0^\infty e^{-z/b} \, dz / (2b)$, and $\int_0^\infty e^{-z/b} \, dz = b$.
nodes.title: The Laplace density integrates to one

nodes.summary: For $b > 0$ the Laplace law $\mathrm{Lap}(m, b)$ has total mass $1$, since its density integrates to one.
nodes.title: The Laplace law is a probability measure

nodes.summary: For $b > 0$, $\mathrm{Lap}(m, b) \le e^{|m - m'| / b} \, \mathrm{Lap}(m', b)$ as measures: integrate the pointwise density bound over any measurable set.

nodes.summary: The Laplace law $\mathrm{Lap}(m, b)$ is the measure on $\mathbb{R}$ with density $z \mapsto \exp(-|z - m| / b) / (2b)$ with respect to Lebesgue measure.
